title: RVA to file offset
description:
Write `rvaToOffset(sections, rva)`, which converts a relative virtual address into a file offset using a PE file's section table.

An RVA belongs to a section when it is at least the section's `virtualAddress` and less than `virtualAddress + max(virtualSize, rawSize)`. The file offset is `rva - virtualAddress + pointerToRawData`.

But a section's file data only covers `rawSize` bytes: if the RVA is inside the section but at or beyond `virtualAddress + rawSize`, it is zero-filled memory with no file data, so return `std::nullopt`. Also return `std::nullopt` for an RVA in no section.

The sections may be given in any order.

```
.text   VA 0x1000  vsize 0x3A10  raw 0x3C00 at 0x400
.data   VA 0x5000  vsize 0x2000  raw 0x200  at 0x4000
rvaToOffset(0x1234) = 0x634
rvaToOffset(0x5100) = 0x4100
rvaToOffset(0x5300) = nullopt      (beyond .data's file data)
```
hints: `std::optional<T>` (from `<optional>`) holds either a `T` or nothing. `return value;` gives back a filled one and `return std::nullopt;` an empty one. A caller tests it with `if (result)` (or `result.has_value()`) and reads the value inside with `*result`.
For each section, compute where it ends in memory: its virtual address plus the larger of its two sizes. If the RVA is inside, it belongs to that section.
Within the section, the distance `rva - virtualAddress` must also be less than `rawSize` for there to be bytes in the file.
